evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/documents/DocumentDetailScreen.tsx:118 — the open-document failure path raises `Alert.alert('Could not open document', 'The file viewer is unavailable on this device.')` with hardcoded English strings. The rest of the screen is fully internationalised (it uses `t('documents.detailLoadError')`, `t('documents.notFound')`, `t('common.retry')`, `t('common.loading')` etc.), so non-English users see an untranslated error. Fix: route both strings through react-i18next `t(...)` (e.g. `t('documents.openFailedTitle')` / `t('documents.openFailedBody')`) and add the keys to the locale bundles.

This is the only user-facing string in DocumentDetailScreen.tsx not wrapped in `t()` — the screen already imports `useTranslation` and uses `t` throughout, so this is an isolated i18n regression on the error branch.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/settings/WidgetSettingsScreen.tsx:66 — `Alert.alert('Widget Added', `${widgetMeta?.name ?? type} widget has been configured.`)` and line 79 `Alert.alert('Widgets Updated', 'All widgets have been refreshed.')` use hardcoded English titles and bodies. The screen imports `useTranslation` and already calls `t('common.loading')` (line 92), so these two confirmation Alerts are i18n gaps — non-English users get untranslated success toasts. Fix: wrap all four literals in `t(...)` with interpolation for the widget name (e.g. `t('widgets.addedBody', { name })`) and add the keys to the locale files.
Both call sites are in the widget add / refresh success handlers, i.e. reachable on normal user interaction, not a dev-only path.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/help/FeedbackScreen.tsx:216 — `Alert.alert('Diagnostic Report', diagnosticReport)` uses a hardcoded English title. This screen is otherwise heavily internationalised (26 `t('...')` call sites, including its other Alerts at lines 64/69/75 which use `t('common.error')` + `t('errors.*')`), so the diagnostic-report dialog title is an isolated i18n gap. The body (`diagnosticReport`) is raw diagnostic text and may legitimately stay untranslated, but the title should go through `t(...)` (e.g. `t('feedback.diagnosticReportTitle')`).
